resources.text: Reed-bed count card. Reports O1 and O2 each list three birds. A popular comment says "same place, so obviously duplicates". The form has already accepted an initial upload.

card/voice.text: Nia coordinates a volunteer bird count. She enjoys small observations and is comfortable saying a record is uncertain. She asks for concrete observations without testing or shaming beginners.

history_samples.text: The robin inspected every sandwich. None passed whatever test it was running.
Was it before or after you crossed the bridge? A rough time is fine if you did not write it down.
I have changed my note to “unidentified gull”. The photo does not show enough for the name I first used.

card/reports.text: O1: three birds 07:10–07:25, volunteer Lin. O2: three birds 07:25–07:40, volunteer Bo. Both at reed bed E. Do not infer two independent flocks from summed report fields.

card/files.text: O1 image IMG71, capture07:14. O2 attachment is a forwarded copy of IMG71, capture07:14, uploaded07:32. O2 explicitly says "used Lin's photo, mine was blurred"; no independent visual count is claimed there.

card/protocol.text: Use maximum simultaneously supported birds for consecutive observations at one patch unless independent evidence supports additional individuals. Keep separate volunteer effort intervals; photo reuse is recorded, not a reason to erase a person's effort or invent fraud.

card/bo.text: I was there after Lin. My photo was blurred, so I labelled hers as reused. Please keep my observation time.

title: The two sightings at the same reed bed
task: D1 17:00. I coordinate our volunteer bird count. We announced six reed warblers from two reports. Please check whether the same photo was uploaded twice, correct the table we actually submitted and our public explanation, and preserve the observation effort and volunteer credit. Matching place names alone are no reason to delete an uncertain sighting.
